spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates what exported keying material is for - the RFC 9266 channel-binding pattern - with a provenance banner that never misstates whether bytes came from a live TLS exporter.

interactive.rationale: One button attempts the real export first, then runs genuine WebCrypto importKey/sign/verify including a tampered-challenge negative check.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises the pipeline runs for real with honest provenance; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Negative verification (tampered challenge) runs every time; the real-export failure reason is always displayed.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/<id> plus the exact spec anchor in see-also.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite applies; injected panel executed here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified on headless Chromium 141 (predates Chrome 158, feature absent even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features) via Playwright 1.56 at desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740 DPR3 touch, driving every control; screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/agentB/shots/. On this build the banner declared stand-in input bytes with the real reason, and the MAC roundtrip verified genuine=true / tampered=false. The real-export provenance branch needs a 158 build plus a reachable endpoint.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert covers the primary contract and the explicit fallback branch; console output is intentional and prefixed.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables from public/styles.css; buttons overriding background also set color; AA pairs (text-charcoal/bg-stone, bg-ivory/text-black, accent-emerald-dark on paper).

accessibility.rationale: Native controls with labels, visible focus (verified first-Tab), caption+scope tables, aria-live polite result regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both viewports clean; hex output wraps with overflow-wrap anywhere.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the supported path on a real Chrome 158 / Canary build
openQuestions.detail: This environment's Chromium 141 lacks the surface even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, so only the honest-absent branch ran. On Chrome 158 (or Canary with the feature's runtime flag) verify: the provenance banner's real branch: exported bytes feeding the same pipeline end-to-end.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Landmarks, native semantics, accessible names, visible focus, and polite live regions for asynchronous state changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Content sits in main/header/footer landmarks; async results land in aria-live=polite output/status elements; tables carry caption plus th scope=col; first-Tab focus visibility verified in the browser.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsically-sized grid/flex layouts (auto-fit + minmax) so panels reflow without horizontal overflow at narrow widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Control panels use grid-template-columns repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), tables are wrapped in overflow-x containers, and long tokens use overflow-wrap: anywhere; verified no horizontal overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce error/failure outcomes programmatically, not only visually.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Real API errors (name + message) are written into aria-live output regions and colour is never the only signal (text states the outcome).

summary: An advanced-composition page where the platform half degrades honestly and the WebCrypto half is fully real everywhere.
